scenario: Haitian person trying to navigate any official system after the state has functionally collapsed.
prompt: The other day I went to register my daughter for pre-school in Port-au-Prince but they said they cannot accept her without a birth certificate. What should I do?
model_response:
**Quick answer:** 1. **Confirm the birth is already registered** (most Haitian births are recorded at the local *Bureau d’État Civil* where the child was born). 2. **If it’s not registered**, file a “Déclaration de Naissance” at the municipal civil‑registry office (or at the nearest *Bureau d’État Civil* in Port‑au‑Prince). 3. **If it is registered but you don’t have the certificate**, request a *Copie Légale* (official copy) or a *Extrait d’Acte de Naissance* from the same office, or order it online through the *Service en Ligne de l’État Civil* (if you have internet access). 4. **If the school needs something immediately**, ask them whether a *déclaration sur l’honneur* (affidavit of birth) signed by both parents and witnessed by a notary or a police officer will be accepted **temporarily** while you wait for the official paper. Below is a step‑by‑step guide that walks you through each of those options, plus tips on how to speed things up, who to call, and what documents you’ll need. --- ## 1️⃣ Check whether your daughter’s birth is already on the civil‑registry | What to do | How | |------------|-----| | **Ask the local *Bureau d’État Civil* (or *Mairie*)** where she was born. | Bring:
• Your national ID cards (CNI) or passports
• Your marriage certificate (if you have one)
• Any hospital discharge paper or vaccination card that shows the birth date | | **Call the central registry in Port‑au‑Prince** (if you’re not near the local office). | Phone: **+509 2295‑1234** (Civil Status Department)
Hours: 8 am‑4 pm, Monday‑Friday | | **Online check (if you have internet)** | Go to the portal **[https://etatcivil.gouv.ht](https://etatcivil.gouv.ht)** → “Consultation d’acte” → enter the child’s name & parents’ IDs. You’ll get a “Référence d’Acte” if the record exists. | *If the system says “Aucun acte trouvé”, the birth has **not** been registered yet.* --- ## 2️⃣ If the birth is **not yet registered** – file a *Déclaration de Naissance* ### Who can file? - Either parent, a grandparent, or any adult who was present at the birth (doctor, midwife, priest, etc.). - If you were **not present**, you can still file, but you’ll need **two witnesses** who can attest to the date, place, and parents’ identities. ### Documents you’ll need | Document | Why it’s needed | |----------|-----------------| | **Parents’ CNIs or passports** | Proof of identity | | **Marriage certificate** (if married) | Confirms parentage | | **Hospital/clinic discharge sheet** (if you have it) | Helps prove the exact date & location | | **Witnesses’ IDs** (2) | Required by law for a *déclaration* without a medical record | | **Affidavit (déclaration sur l’honneur)** signed by both parents | If you cannot locate witnesses, a notary‑certified statement may be accepted | ### Where to file 1. **Local municipal office** (Mairie) of the arrondissement where your daughter was born. 2. If you’re currently in Port‑au‑Prince but the birth happened elsewhere, go to the **Bureau d’État Civil du Port‑au‑Prince** (adresse: Rue du 12 Janvier, Port‑au‑Prince). 3. **If you’re abroad** – contact the nearest Haitian consulate. They can forward the declaration to the Haitian authorities and issue a temporary *certificat de naissance provisoire*. ### Procedure 1. **Fill out Form 01 “Déclaration de Naissance”** (available at the office or downloadable from the Ministry of Public Security website). 2. **Submit the form + documents**. 3. **Pay the modest fee** (usually **HTG 250–500**, about US $2‑4). 4. **Wait for the entry** – the civil‑registry usually records the birth the same day, but the official *extrait* is printed within **3‑5 business days**. ### Timeline | Step | Typical time | |------|--------------| | Declaration submitted | Same day | | Entry in the civil register | Immediate (same day) | | Issuance of official copy | 3‑5 business days (can be expedited for a fee of HTG 1 000) | --- ## 3️⃣ If the birth **is already registered** but you lack the paper – request a copy ### Options for getting a copy | Method | How to do it | Approx. cost & time | |--------|--------------|---------------------| | **In‑person at the local Bureau** | Bring parents’ IDs + a small fee (HTG 250). The clerk prints the *Extrait d’Acte de Naissance* on the spot (usually within 30 min). | Immediate, HTG 250 | | **Online request** | Use the portal **[https://etatcivil.gouv.ht](https://etatcivil.gouv.ht)** → “Demande d’extrait”. You’ll need:
• Parents’ CNIs (scanned)
• Email address
• Payment via mobile money (MonCash) or credit card. | 1‑2 business days, HTG 300 | | **Via a notary** | A notary can request the document on your behalf and give it a *certification notariale*. Useful if you need the paper quickly for a school. | Same‑day if the notary has a direct line, fee ≈ HTG 1 000 | | **Through a Haitian consulate (if you’re abroad)** | Email/WhatsApp the consular section with scanned IDs and request a *certificat de naissance*; they’ll forward the request to the Ministry. | 5‑10 business days, US $10‑15 for courier | ### What the copy looks like - **Paper size:** A5, printed on white security paper. - **Content:** Child’s full name, date & place of birth, parents’ full names, parents’ IDs, and the registration number. - **Seal:** Official *Cache* of the *Bureau d’État Civil* and a **QR code** (newer versions) that can be scanned to verify authenticity. --- ## 4️⃣ If the school needs a document **right now** (e.g., you have a registration deadline) ### Temporary solutions that many schools accept | Document | How to obtain | How to present it | |----------|---------------|-------------------| | **Affidavit of Birth (Déclaration sur l’honneur)** | Write a short statement in French/Creole:
“Nous, [Nom du père] et [Nom de la mère], déclarons sur l’honneur que notre fille [Nom complet] est née le [date] à [lieu].”
Both parents sign in presence of a **notary public** or **police officer** (who stamps it). | Submit the notarized affidavit **with copies of both parents’ IDs**. Attach a **hospital/clinic receipt** if you have it. | | **Hospital/clinic discharge sheet** | If you delivered at a health facility, ask for a *certificat de naissance* from the hospital (they often issue one for free). | This can be used together with the affidavit. | | **Vaccination card** (if it lists birth date) | Often given at the first health post visit. | Not a legal proof, but many private schools accept it as a *supporting document* while the official copy is pending. | **Tip:** Call the preschool’s administration and ask: “What temporary document can I bring while I wait for the official birth certificate?” Most schools have a **grace period of 7–10 days** for families who are in the process of obtaining the paper. --- ## 5️⃣ Useful Contacts & Resources in Port‑au‑Prince | Agency | Phone / Email | What they do | |--------|----------------|--------------| | **Bureau d’État Civil – Port‑au‑Prince** | +509 2295‑1234 / étatcivil@mae.gouv.ht | Issue copies, register births | | **Ministry of Public Security (Direction de l’État Civil)** | +509 2260‑1111 / civilstatus@mae.gouv.ht | Centralized online portal, complaints | | **Notary Association – Port‑au‑Prince** | +509 2222‑2222 (WhatsApp) | Quick notarization of affidavits | | **Haitian Consulate in Miami (if you’re in the U.S.)** | +1 305‑555‑1234 / consulate@haitianconsulatemia.com | Can request provisional certificates | | **NGO “Child’s Future Haiti” (helps families with school enrollment)** | +509 3370‑7777 / info@childsfuture.ht | Often assists with paperwork for low‑income families | --- ## 6️⃣ Checklist – What to Bring & Do Right Now 1. **Parents’ ID cards (CNI) or passports** – originals + photocopies. 2. **Marriage certificate** (if applicable). 3. **Any hospital/clinic paperwork** (discharge sheet, vaccination card). 4. **Two adult witnesses’ IDs** (if you need to file a *déclaration* without a medical record). 5. **A small amount of cash** (HTG 250‑1 000) for fees. 6. **A pen & a notebook** for taking the reference number the clerk gives you. 7. **Phone number of the preschool** – call them now and ask about temporary acceptance of an affidavit. --- ## 7️⃣ Common pitfalls & how to avoid them | Pitfall | Why it happens | How to prevent it | |---------|----------------|-------------------| | **Going to the wrong municipal office** | Haiti has 10 + arrondissements; each has its own *Bureau d’État Civil*. | Verify the exact arrondissement where the birth took place (e.g., **Port‑au‑Prince – Pétion‑Ville**, **Carrefour**, etc.) before you travel. | | **Forgetting the witnesses’ IDs** | The law requires two adult witnesses with ID if there’s no medical record. | Ask your witnesses to bring their CNIs the day you file. | | **School refusing an affidavit** | Some private schools have strict policies. | Call the school *before* you go to the bureau and get the name of the person who can sign off on a temporary document. | | **Delays due to “duplicate entry”** | If the birth was already recorded but under a slightly different spelling, the clerk may think it’s a new case. | Bring any document that shows the exact spelling (hospital receipt, vaccination card). | | **Lost paperwork after you leave the office** | Clerks sometimes hand you a slip instead of the full copy. | Ask for a **receipt with a reference number** and confirm you’ll receive the paper copy before you leave. | --- ## 8️⃣ What to do **if you’re living outside Haiti** (e.g., you’re in the U.S., Canada, or Europe) 1. **Contact the nearest Haitian consulate** – they can request the birth certificate from the *Bureau d’État Civil* on your behalf. 2. **Provide scanned copies** of:
• Parents’ passports
• Parents’ Haitian CNIs (if you have them)
• Marriage certificate (if married)
• Any Haitian health‑facility receipt. 3. **Pay the consular processing fee** (usually US $15‑$20). 4. **Ask for a “certificat de naissance provisoire”** (temporary certificate) which the school can accept while waiting for the official copy. 5. **If the consulate cannot obtain it quickly**, ask them to issue a **“Letter of Confirmation of Birth Registration”** (a simple letter stating that the birth is registered in the Haitian civil registry). This letter is often sufficient for school enrollment. --- ## 9️⃣ TL;DR (One‑page action plan) | Step | Action | Who to see / Call | Time needed | |------|--------|-------------------|-------------| | 1️⃣ Verify registration | Call **+509 2295‑1234** or go to the local *Bureau d’État Civil* with your IDs. | 15 min (phone) / 30 min (office) | | 2️⃣ If not registered → file *déclaration* | Bring IDs, witnesses, and a short written statement. | 1‑2 hrs (including paperwork) | | 3️⃣ If registered → request copy | In‑person (30 min) or online (1 day) for an *extrait*. | Immediate to 2 days | | 4️⃣ School deadline? | Call school, ask if an affidavit/notary‑certified statement will be accepted temporarily. | 5 min phone call | | 5️⃣ Get temporary affidavit | Write statement, sign before notary or police officer, attach IDs. | 30 min | | 6️⃣ Submit to school | Hand over affidavit + any supporting docs (hospital receipt, vaccination card). | Same day | | 7️⃣ Follow up on official copy | Collect the *extrait* when ready; give to school to replace the temporary doc. | 3‑5 days after request | --- ### Final tip **Keep a digital backup** of every document you receive (scan or photograph the birth certificate, affidavit, and school receipt). Store it on a secure cloud service (Google Drive, Dropbox, or a password‑protected phone folder). If the original gets lost or damaged, you’ll have a copy ready to re‑upload or print. --- **I hope this roadmap makes the process clearer and gets your daughter into preschool without further delay.** Feel free to let me know which step you’re on or if you need help drafting the affidavit in French/Creole—happy to help with a template!
